newsitem.title: UK: VLCC rates slip despite fair enquiry levels.
newsitem.headline: VLCC rates slip despite fair enquiry levels.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates showed signs of slipping on Friday despite reasonable enquiry levels, brokers said.

"Despite the fact that most of the eastbound Gulf cargoes have been loading within the next three weeks, and the list of available tonnage has been gradually slimming down, there has been a perceivable lack of confidence among owners that they are in any position to stop a decline in rates," said brokers Galbraith's Ltd in their weekly tanker report.
Mideast/Japan voyages were fixed at about W67.5/70 against W72.5 earlier in the week and a year high earlier this month of W75, while modern vessels to the U.S. Gulf dipped to around W52.5.
In addition the 275,000 tonne Sebu was done at $2.3 million on a Norway/China trip for Statoil, while from West Africa to Taiwan the 245,000 tonne Pacific Jewel was fixed at W57.5 for CPC.

The West Africa Suezmax (130,000 tonne) sector was quiet and rates fell about five points to around W85, while in the Med W90/92.5 continued to be achieved for modern ships and around W85 for older vessels.

Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) in the Med, which shot up to W160 earlier in the week, were lifeless on Friday with rates difficult to assess. In the North Sea tonnage was tight, keeping levels at a healthy W125 despite low activity, brokers said.
Caribs/upcoast crude rates were little changed over the week at W70 for 70,000 tonnes. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
